messages:
support-bot: Escalation created for AcmePay (Dedicated). Customer reports 429s + intermittent 500s starting ~2024-11-02 11:28 UTC after switching to long-context prompts. cc @maria @aj :eyes:

maria: On it — customer says the spike correlates with requests containing >60k context (chat history + docs). They see timeouts first, then spikes of 429s. Any quick mitigations?

aj: Pushed initial metrics — eviction rate jumped sharply at 11:27:45. CPU and GPU load look fine. Memory fragmentation and KV slab churn are through the roof. Tagging @jamal for allocator/infra view.

sre-bot: Recent logs from runtime (excerpt):
```
[11:27:41] kvcache: evict start tenant=acmepay evicts=12
[11:27:42] kvcache: slab_realloc: split_slab id=0x7f3a size=524288 -> fragmentation=0.68
[11:27:45] runtime: req=abcd1234 latency=1800ms status=429 cause=kvcache-throttle
[11:27:46] kvcache: evict burst rate=4200 evicts/s
[11:27:47] allocator: backlog=342 reassigns=87
```

jamal: This looks like slab reallocation thrash. Long-context workloads are forcing many large KV entries, splitting slabs and fragmenting free space. The allocator is spending cycles moving pages which blocks cache ops -> queue growth -> request-level throttling. Repro is possible with our longctx harness.

liam: I reproduced locally: run the longctx-harness with 20 concurrent sessions, each pushing ~70k tokens history at ~2rps. Results: eviction storm + 429s in ~90s. Repro steps I used: 
```
# repro (local harness)
./longctx-harness --tenant acmepay --concurrency 20 --prompt-size 70k --rate 2
```
Mitigations that helped in my run: toggle background compaction and reduce per-tenant soft_limit to 60%.

maria: Customer is asking about immediate workarounds and billing credits — they hit a lot of retries and billable tokens. Suggested message: pause batch jobs, reduce context length, and we can offer a short credit while we remediate. I'll draft.

aj: Quick temporary server-side toggles we can apply for this tenant: enable KV compaction and lower soft limit. Example admin API call: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/dedicated/admin/tenants/ACME_ID/config
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
 -H "Content-Type: application/json"
 -d '{"kv_cache.compaction":"on","kv_cache.soft_limit":"0.6"}'
```
I also recommend throttling heavy routes for 10m while we observe.

jamal: Plan: 1) apply compaction + soft limit change to tenant (canary) 2) if eviction rate doesn't fall, roll a rolling restart of that GPU pool to reclaim fragmented memory pages (15m canary) 3) collect heap/slab maps and feed to allocator team for tuning.

liam: Long-term: allocator needs a background compaction task and lower slab-split threshold for multi-tenant Dedicated. I opened RFC infra/allocator PR-132 to propose: background_compactor, slab_split_pct=0.45, and per-tenant compaction windows.

maria: I'm messaging the customer with suggested mitigations and ETA for our canary actions. Also opened SR-58934 to track billing relief request.

aj: Executing step 1 now (compaction on + soft_limit 0.6) for ACME_ID. Monitoring eviction/latency dashboards. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Metric snapshot after toggle (11:40 UTC):
```
evict_rate: 4200 -> 850 evicts/s
median_latency: 780ms -> 240ms
429_count: 320 -> 18
fragmentation: 68% -> 52% (initial)
```

jamal: Good sign. I'll keep the pool on watch for 30m. If we see reaccumulation we'll proceed with rolling restart.

maria: Customer updated. They accepted temporary throttling of their heavy routes and appreciated the fast response. I'll follow up about credits once we have full timeline.

liam: Filed follow-ups: allocator tuning + add longctx smoke tests to Dedicated CI.

aj: Action items: jamal -> keep monitoring and escalate to restart if needed. liam -> RFC + perf tests. maria -> customer comms and billing ticket. I'll close this Slack thread after 1h if stable.

sre-bot: If throttles persist beyond 20m, this will be promoted to #incidents and a postmortem will be scheduled.
